channel.title: onlinefdr.com.au blog
channel.description: Plain-language, statute-accurate guidance on Family Dispute Resolution, parenting, and property settlement under the Family Law Act 1975.

item.title: How much does a divorce cost in Australia?
item.description: A divorce costs about $1,100 to file in Australia. The real money is in property and parenting, where your path can swing it by tens of thousands.

item.title: Do grandparents have a right to see their grandchildren in Australia?
item.description: Grandparents have no automatic right to see grandchildren in Australia, but they can apply for a parenting order, and usually must try mediation first.

item.title: Can you change final parenting orders in Australia?
item.description: Final parenting orders can be changed by agreement anytime, or through a court only if there's been a significant change of circumstances since they were made.

item.title: Can you get spousal maintenance after separating in Australia?
item.description: Spousal maintenance is Australia's version of alimony: support for a former partner who cannot yet support themselves. Who qualifies and how it works.

item.title: Is technology-facilitated abuse a form of family violence in Australia?
item.description: Technology-facilitated abuse, such as tracking and monitoring, is a recognised form of family violence under Australian law. What it is and where to get help.

item.title: Does family violence affect a property settlement in Australia?
item.description: How the 2025 family law changes make the effect of family violence a required consideration in an Australian property settlement, and how it works in mediation.

item.title: If your ex breaks a parenting order, do you have to go back to mediation first?
item.description: If your ex breaks a parenting order, you usually must attempt Family Dispute Resolution first, unless a recent serious breach meets a section 60I exemption.

item.title: Can the court still add back money your ex spent in a property settlement?
item.description: Add-backs largely ended on 10 June 2025. Under section 79(3) the court divides only property that still exists, and Shinohara 2025 confirmed it.

item.title: Can a parent take a child interstate or overseas without the other parent's consent?
item.description: Moving a child interstate is not automatically banned in Australia, but taking a child overseas can be a criminal offence where parenting orders apply.

item.title: Can you be separated while living in the same house?
item.description: Yes, you can be separated while living in the same house in Australia, but you need proof the relationship was genuinely over, including two affidavits for divorce.

item.title: How long after separating can you get divorced in Australia?
item.description: You must be separated at least 12 months before applying for divorce in Australia. The extra hurdles for short marriages were removed on 10 June 2025.

item.title: Can you do family dispute resolution if English is not your first language?
item.description: Yes. Online family dispute resolution can be run in your own language using live AI translated captions in Google Meet, which now support 69 languages.

item.title: How "best interests of the child" actually works after the 2024 amendments
item.description: Section 60CC of the Family Law Act was rewritten on 6 May 2024. Here is how the new six-factor best-interests test actually works in 2026, factor by factor.

item.title: What is the duty of disclosure in financial settlement, and how does it work after the 2024 amendments?
item.description: The duty of full and frank financial disclosure now sits in sections 71B, 90RI, and 90YJA of the Family Law Act 1975. Statutory anchors and case law.

item.title: Section 60I certificate vs Genuine Steps Certificate: what each is and when you need which
item.description: A Section 60I certificate is FDRP-issued for parenting only; a Genuine Steps Certificate is party-signed for every application. Statutory anchors explained.

item.title: At what age can a child decide which parent to live with in Australia?
item.description: There is no age in Australian family law at which a child can decide which parent to live with. What Section 60CC and the High Court of Australia actually say.

item.title: What 'genuine effort' means in Family Dispute Resolution
item.description: What genuine effort means in Family Dispute Resolution, what counts and what does not, and how the certificate type can affect later court proceedings.

item.title: Who keeps the family pet after separation? Companion animals under the 2024 reforms
item.description: What the Family Law Amendment Act 2024 changed about pets after separation in Australia. Companion animal status, factors the court considers, and shared care.

item.title: When your child says they don't want to go to the other parent's house
item.description: What Australian family law says when a child resists time with the other parent. How children's views are weighed, and what parents should do next.

item.title: How superannuation splitting works after separation in Australia
item.description: Learn how superannuation splitting works in Australian family law property settlements, including the 4-step process, Consent Orders, and duty of disclosure.

item.title: How the 2026 budget CGT changes impact your property settlement
item.description: Understand how the 2026 Federal Budget CGT and negative gearing changes affect Australian family law property settlements and trust distributions.
